assumptions: Membrane tracer illustrates a possible passive inward route under suitable driving conditions, not a stochastic trajectory or calculated ion voltage. Only lipid and a specific sodium channel are shown; other carriers, pumps and endocytosis omitted. Icons not molecular sizes.

Diffusion uses 16 independent point walkers on a 24x12 lattice. Each random proposal chooses four cardinal directions with equal probability, independent of concentration. At outer edges proposals stay put. Equal-volume halves have an imaginary count boundary, no membrane. Point overlaps allowed. Seven snapshots at 32-step intervals; no thermal, solvent-flow or physical-time/rate calculation. Seeded replay repeats a trace. Crossing events include repeated returns and conserve counts.

Osmosis illustrates initial net water tendency at equal temperature/pressure with relatively impermeant solutes and an optionally water-permeable membrane. Both directions occur if water passage exists. Shape changes are qualitative, not calculated endpoints. Initial relative solute concentrations are 1/4/8 outside versus 4 inside. No pressure feedback, final volume/concentration or real time is calculated. Wall support/turgor can limit later net influx.

Geometric boxes have total volume 8 invented units cubed. All six exposed faces counted, including unseen faces. Eight small cubes are separated, not a touching cluster. Centre-to-nearest-face distance is one geometric measure, not all diffusion paths or time. No exchange rate, survival or actual cell dimensions predicted.

Juice can also mix by currents; salted vegetables can be affected by tissue damage. Familiar appearances do not independently establish a sole mechanism. No cutting, chemicals, sampling or changed plant care needed.

references.use: Passive routes, diffusion, osmosis and plant turgor
